statusMeaning.supported: Evidence supports the stated diagnostic or research intervention; this does not mean a trading edge is proven.
statusMeaning.rejected: The stated promotion or sufficiency claim conflicts with cited evidence for the specified candidate/sample.
statusMeaning.needs_data: Plausible, explicitly unvalidated candidate or comparison requiring a new replay and/or prospective evidence.

scope: Unlevered funded spot alternatives and model-selection evidence. Root owns market replays; this agent independently recalculated concentration, neighboring-parameter and passive-excess diagnostics from root screen ledgers.

recommendedBoundedFamily.status: Pre-screen strategy nomination preserved; superseded for research priority by root development-locked ETH40 candidate after independent result review.

hypotheses.title: Use cash as the absolute net-profit benchmark
hypotheses.rationale: All three previously frozen daily candidates lost in the 2026 comparison. Avoiding loss is useful, but zero-trade cash behavior does not meet the profit objective.
hypotheses.testability: Replay cash at the same starting capital and exact calendar dates; report net dollars and activity separately.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Prevents a least-losing candidate from being presented as a profitable winner; creates no returns itself.

hypotheses.title: Use costed BTC buy-and-hold as the passive opportunity-cost benchmark
hypotheses.rationale: Earlier weekly trend earned less total dollars than its passive BTC comparator while reducing sampled drawdown. Positive model dollars alone do not establish value added.
hypotheses.testability: Start both policies with cash, the same funded initial exposure and execution convention; separately disclose later exposure differences and risk-adjusted comparisons.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Separates market appreciation from useful timing; passive exposure can lose substantially.

hypotheses.title: Retain exact 40-week BTC trend as a nominated slow baseline
hypotheses.rationale: The existing weekly study shows +1175.60 USD base and +1228.51 USD stress over 2017 through September 2026, 11 episodes, but its bootstrap lower mean weekly net is -0.48 USD. It is promising historical evidence, not validated future expectancy.
hypotheses.testability: Exact formula: SMA40 on completed native weeks; enter above SMA*1.0166, exit at/below SMA, preserve state in band. Replay with sufficient pre-period weekly warmup and identical comparator accounting; then assess newly collected outcomes.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Low turnover can reduce cost drag and avoid some prolonged bear exposure, at the price of late entries and exits.

hypotheses.title: BTC-only majority trend across three horizons with symmetric hysteresis
hypotheses.rationale: Thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day trends can disagree; a fixed majority could reduce dependence on one crossover. This is a new economic hypothesis and a bounded alternative to the failed drift and rotation predictors.
hypotheses.testability: Freeze SMA windows [30,60,90], count close>SMA*(1+b) and close<SMA/(1+b), enter on two upper votes and exit on two lower votes, preserve state otherwise; b is the exact declared base round-trip reference-price break-even move. Require 90 completed bars, delayed funded fills, no additions. No post-result parameter search.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: May reduce whipsaw and switching fees; can also miss early recovery and retain losses. Net direction is unknown.
hypotheses.rootScreenNote: Related consensus_btc-090 lost in later windows, with a different lower-band formula. Exact S04 remains untested; ETH40 has stronger current exploratory evidence.

hypotheses.title: Single BTC SMA90 with the same symmetric band as a complexity control
hypotheses.rationale: If a single fixed trend performs as well as the majority rule, ensemble complexity has no demonstrated benefit.
hypotheses.testability: Use the same costs, warmup, execution, entry/exit band and exposure as S04, replacing the majority with one SMA90 vote. Declare this as one additional tested variant.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Identifies whether horizon averaging adds economic value rather than merely more parameters.

hypotheses.title: Asymmetric Donchian breakout as an alternative trend entry mechanism
hypotheses.rationale: A prior-price breakout asks whether trend continuation follows a range escape, unlike moving-average distance. No proof follows from that interpretation.
hypotheses.testability: For a later separate experiment freeze BTC close above the prior 120 completed daily closes maximum for entry; exit below the prior 60-close minimum. Exclude the decision close from both reference windows. Charge the same costs and delayed fills.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Potentially very low turnover and persistent upside participation; can enter near exhausted moves.

hypotheses.title: Reduce trend exposure when trailing volatility rises
hypotheses.rationale: Primary research supports volatility management in other asset classes; transfer to crypto and tiny funded spot allocations is unestablished.
hypotheses.testability: In a separate frozen sizing experiment compute trailing 30-day realized volatility and only reduce the existing entry budget via a fixed capped inverse-volatility multiplier. Never increase above current authorized cap; account for minimum size and any rebalance costs.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: May reduce drawdown; lower exposure can also reduce profits. It does not repair negative signal expectancy.

hypotheses.title: Require persistent exit-and-reentry separation to suppress churn
hypotheses.rationale: A fixed cooldown after a trend exit can reduce repeated loss-making crossings but may miss rapid recoveries. Prior momentum literature documents regime-dependent losses.
hypotheses.testability: Apply a predeclared seven-completed-day reentry cooldown to one frozen candidate in a separate ablation; exits remain immediate at the signal horizon. Log missed qualifying entries and final mark-outs.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Trades fewer noisy reversals but carries meaningful opportunity cost; unknown net benefit.

hypotheses.title: Promote the already-tested BTC/ETH 60-day rotation
hypotheses.rationale: The preselected rotation earned +461.59 USD in 2025 H2 validation, concentrated in one ETH winner, then lost -98.00 USD base and -159.49 USD combined stress in 2026.
hypotheses.testability: Retain original frozen module and ledgers as a failed reference; retrying alternate windows requires registering a new trial and new evidence.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Present evidence does not justify replacing the active policy with this candidate.

hypotheses.title: Monthly rather than daily relative-strength decisions
hypotheses.rationale: The failed rotation incurred entry and switching costs. A fixed monthly decision schedule tests whether slower cross-sectional allocation has a better net tradeoff without adding assets.
hypotheses.testability: For a later study hold between month-end decisions; compare BTC and ETH on predeclared 90-day momentum, require positive own momentum, retain incumbent unless the candidate advantage exceeds one declared round-trip hurdle. Same-date costed benchmarks are mandatory.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Less switching may save fees but slower exits and just two correlated assets limit diversification.

hypotheses.title: Fixed BTC/ETH basket without routine rebalancing
hypotheses.rationale: A simple funded basket is a baseline for claiming that choosing between BTC and ETH adds value. It requires neither a predictive model nor frequent rotation.
hypotheses.testability: Split one total allowed entry budget equally at inception, charge both assets fees, preserve fixed units, mark all liquidation costs, and compare on identical dates. Requires an explicitly multi-position research accountant.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: May diversify asset-specific performance; common crypto market exposure can still dominate losses.

hypotheses.title: Broader liquid-asset cross-sectional momentum
hypotheses.rationale: Research finds crypto market, size and momentum factors, but broader long-short results do not establish a funded long-only BTC/ETH edge. A wider point-in-time universe is a materially different data project.
hypotheses.testability: Obtain point-in-time listings, delistings, liquidity and historical tradability. Freeze universe eligibility before returns; include failed/delisted assets and realistic volume/cost limits. No current-survivor-only scan.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Could add independent opportunities; survivorship and small-asset execution costs can erase apparent advantage.

hypotheses.title: Declare a blend of the three failed daily candidates profitable
hypotheses.rationale: A convex combination of their separately funded 2026 return streams remains negative when every component has negative net return. Combining target signals is a different untested strategy.
hypotheses.testability: For accounting blends aggregate synchronized component P&L with fixed nonnegative weights summing to one; for signal combinations register a separate causal replay with actual turnover.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Diversification can reduce variance but cannot change the sign of the fixed convex weighted net totals in this sample.

hypotheses.title: Promote the fitted OU residual reversion candidate
hypotheses.rationale: The patient variant did not trade during development and lost -186.39 USD base and -218.82 USD combined stress in the 2026 comparison. The other development variants also lost.
hypotheses.testability: Keep all four declared variants and rejection diagnostics; do not replace failed stability or excursion filters merely to induce entries.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Current tested reversion family offers no supported profit solution.

hypotheses.title: Simple pullback entry inside an established rising trend
hypotheses.rationale: A trend-filtered pullback trades temporary weakness while avoiding explicit AR(1) estimation, so it is distinct from the rejected OU fit. No local evidence yet establishes that the discount predicts recovery.
hypotheses.testability: Later freeze BTC close above SMA90 and a trailing five-day loss greater than a declared volatility-scaled amount; exit after recovery to prior level or fixed holding limit. Compare against trend entry without pullback selection on the same dates.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Potentially improves entry price; may systematically buy the beginning of structural declines.

hypotheses.title: Require out-of-sample residual stability before any pairs/reversion strategy
hypotheses.rationale: A fitted half-life is conditional on a locally stable process. Price ratios can trend and the prior OU model already rejected many nonstationary or falling samples.
hypotheses.testability: Estimate residual relationships only on past data, report coefficient and half-life stability on subsequent blocks, and count model invalidations. Funded spot rotation must not be labelled market-neutral pairs arbitrage.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Avoids interpreting an unstable fit as a guaranteed restoring force; does not independently create a tradeable edge.

hypotheses.title: Promote CUSUM change detection as a return forecast
hypotheses.rationale: The selected CUSUM lost -16.95 USD in 2026 with only one entry and no strategy exit. It also lost during development. Detecting a drift change and predicting profitable future drift are separate claims.
hypotheses.testability: Preserve frozen signal as a failed reference and distinguish strategy exits from terminal liquidation; a new prediction calibration requires subsequent labeled observations.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Smallest observed loss is not sufficient evidence of profitable predictability.

hypotheses.title: Return to the previously failed hourly trend system
hypotheses.rationale: The frozen hourly trend screen lost -1021.72 USD base during 2024 development and -803.78 USD base during 2025 H1, with hundreds of trades. Funding alignment checks did not change the conclusion.
hypotheses.testability: Use its immutable replay as evidence of the tested design failure; any substantially changed signal needs a new registered trial and executable spot evidence.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: More evaluations and more trades did not establish net profit in that tested system.

hypotheses.title: Treat distance from moving average as a predicted profit margin
hypotheses.rationale: The active specification explicitly says its 1.66% band reduces turnover and is not expected profit. Backward-looking distance gives no calibrated distribution of subsequent liquidation proceeds.
hypotheses.testability: Separate signal-strength fields from empirical forward net-return estimates; only label expected net edge after evaluation on later realized executable outcomes.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Prevents a numerical hurdle from falsely appearing to guarantee fee recovery.

hypotheses.title: Assume lower fees alone will make the failed daily candidates profitable
hypotheses.rationale: At zero commissions but retained adverse execution, 2026 net remained -1.10 USD CUSUM, -141.53 USD reversion and -35.48 USD rotation. Costs worsen an already adverse price outcome.
hypotheses.testability: Keep identical signal paths and delay while changing fees only; separate actual account tier verification from hypothetical zero-cost diagnostics. Never assume passive orders fill.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Confirms signal quality must improve as well as cost efficiency for these frozen paths.

hypotheses.title: Calibrate decision horizons against realized executable net movement
hypotheses.rationale: A short horizon is economically unsuitable if favorable future movement rarely covers both sides of costs. Existing daily and hourly failures motivate measuring the attainable net distribution directly.
hypotheses.testability: For every frozen candidate decision, archive contemporaneous quotes, costs, intended horizon and later bid-side liquidation mark-outs at predeclared horizons; retain rejected decisions and account for overlapping outcomes.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Can reject economically impossible horizons and distinguish forecast failure from cost drag; no current positive edge is implied.

hypotheses.title: Measure timing skill against equal-exposure passive returns
hypotheses.rationale: A low-exposure model can show a smaller account drawdown simply because most capital stays in cash. Earlier weekly and daily dollar figures use different starting capital and entry caps.
hypotheses.testability: Report account return, allocated-capital return, average and peak exposure, turnover and net excess vs an explicitly risk/exposure-matched benchmark. Do not compare unadjusted dollars across incompatible studies.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Reveals whether the model improves timing or merely invests less.

hypotheses.title: Track winner concentration and remove the largest trade diagnostically
hypotheses.rationale: Rotation validation had one +544.03 USD ETH episode and one -82.44 USD loss. A result dependent on one episode has weak evidence of repeatable profitability.
hypotheses.testability: Report contribution by episode, asset and regime, plus leave-one-episode-out net and effective independent sample limitations. Do not select models on this diagnostic after seeing final results.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Prevents a lucky concentrated episode from being mistaken for stable expectancy.
hypotheses.rootScreenNote: Independent ETH40 review finds each later window loses when its largest episode is excluded; the 2026 largest episode is forced terminal liquidation.

hypotheses.title: Count every tested variant and reserve a genuinely later evaluation
hypotheses.rationale: Expanding to many agents, hypotheses or variants increases selection opportunities. Historical dates already inspected by previous studies cannot be restored to untouched status by a new split.
hypotheses.testability: Save a trial registry with parameters, code/data hashes and all failures before replay; freeze the candidate and evaluation rules before newly collected data. Use dependence-aware uncertainty and disclose unknown prior search counts.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Reduces false discoveries from model search; is research discipline rather than an alpha source.

hypotheses.title: Promote only after a prospective shadow experiment answers the profit question
hypotheses.rationale: Current local evidence is repeated historical research with sparse episodes. New books and recorded decisions can test actual eligibility and execution without changing existing risk.
hypotheses.testability: Freeze one nominated candidate in isolated research output; record all signals, rejects, fee-inclusive fills, terminal marks and synchronized passive/cash benchmarks on subsequently observed data. Set decision checkpoints in advance and report insufficient evidence when too few independent episodes occur.
hypotheses.likelyImpact: Produces the missing evidence needed to decide whether a strategy makes executable net profit; completion depends on future market observations.
hypotheses.rootScreenNominee: sma_eth-040, as separately frozen prospective research only; existing screen gates failed.
